GN Store Nord: a dated capital return transforms EPS but not the business, so at a fair multiple the return to March 2028 is about +6%, not +130%

GN Store Nord (GN-DK): investment memo, 26 November 2026. Money is in DKK. Definitions of RemainCo, EBITA and the two EPS bases are in the end notes.

#0 Summary of key insights, implications and conclusions

GN is about to stop being a leveraged hearing-aid and headset group and become two assets inside one share. The first asset is a pile of cash and listed securities that GN will turn into fewer shares. The second asset is a cyclical audio-hardware business earning trough margins. The cash asset is contracted, dated and almost independent of demand, and it lifts EPS from about DKK 2 to about DKK 8 in two years. The hardware business decides what those earnings are worth, and it is where the evidence is thinnest and expectations are fullest.

What matters most

1Two assets sit in one share. About DKK 50-55 of each share, roughly 45% of the price, is net cash after closing, 56 million Amplifon shares and a stake in Nations Benefits. The remaining DKK 65-70 values RemainCo at about 11 times 2027 EBITA, which is a full price for the business, not a discount.
2The per-share step-up in EPS is the firm part of the case. About four fifths of the rise in EPS between 2026 and 2028 comes from repaying debt and retiring shares. The step-up needs the Hearing sale to close and shareholders to approve the buyback. It needs no customer to buy anything.
3EPS growth is not value growth. From 2027 to 2030 model EPS compounds at about 30% a year, EBITA at about 10% and net income at about 4%. A buyback done at fair value turns cash into fewer shares and creates no value. Value per share grows only as fast as RemainCo's profit, plus whatever GN gains by buying its shares below intrinsic value.
4The market already has the good news and has left no cushion. Every broker models the sale, the cash, the DKK 4bn return and the DKK 200m cost saving. Consensus 2027 EBITA sits at the bottom of the finance director's range, not below it. The model's operating forecasts are below consensus.
5The skew splits cleanly by line. The skew is positive on capital return, on 2028 EPS, on the dividend and on mechanical EPS upgrades in the next three months. The skew is negative on 2027 revenue and EBITA estimates and on operating guidance, which this management team has cut in every recent year.
6The return depends on the multiple. The model shows +130% to March 2028 at the guideline fair multiple of 24.79x, a multiple that I think belongs to the hearing-aid group GN used to be. At 14-16x like-for-like earnings, about 10 times EBITA, the return is about +6% to March 2028 and about 10% a year over three years, within a range of roughly (31)% to +33%.
7The protection from the cash has an end date. The cash protects the holder until early 2028, while GN spends it on shares. After early 2028 the holder owns a geared claim on a cyclical business.
8Three events would turn GN into a clearly skewed opportunity. First, a guidance reset in February 2027 that sets a bar the company can beat. Second, hard evidence that European demand has turned. Third, a lower entry price: near DKK 100 the buyback retires shares at about 7.5-8 times EBITA, so every krone spent adds value per share.
The model's +130% return to March 2028 rests on the guideline's 24.79x multiple. At 14-16x like-for-like earnings the return is about +6%, and the protection from the cash ends in early 2028.

#1 Tailwinds in the operating environment, and the absence of headwinds

Conclusion: The environment is a trough turning up in two regions on a structurally slower base, so it flatters the next two quarters and does not, by itself, support upgrades.

Evidence.

What is turning up

  • The trough is turning, region by region. Enterprise organic growth was negative for 14 quarters and turned to +1% in Q3 2026. North America and Asia-Pacific grew at double-digit rates early in 2026, and sales out of North American business channels have risen for four quarters. Europe, about half of revenue, fell at double-digit rates in the first half of 2026, and management describes it only as "challenging but improved".
  • The end of destocking helps, but only once. Distributors are finishing their destocking, so GN's sales into the channel will rise to match sales out of it. Higher interest rates keep distributors' stocks permanently lower, so no restocking boom will follow.
  • Trade policy has moved from headwind to neutral. The 2025 US tariffs cost GN about one point of margin. GN has moved its supply chain, the Q3 2026 tariff refund was a one-off, and about 0.3 points of margin drag remains. One US executive order could reverse the improvement.
  • Gaming has near-term help, against a weak European consumer. Grand Theft Auto 6 was released on consoles on 19 November 2026, and Logitech is short of supply this holiday season. European consumer confidence is weak: the German GfK consumer-climate index stands at (30.8).

What still weighs

  • The structural base is slower. Office workers now replace headsets every four to five years, against two to three years before. Chief information officers plan to raise spending on peripherals by 2.0%, and by 0.1% at the largest companies (Morgan Stanley, October 2026).
  • This week's evidence leans the wrong way. PC shipments are forecast to fall 8-11% in 2027 (Jefferies, 25 November 2026). HP guided below consensus on the same day. Logitech's sales out of European channels fell 7% in its September quarter.
  • The investment backdrop is hostile. Viewforth's environment reading rates the sector Underweight and the industry Double Underweight in a risk-off market, and the dashboard rates GN's Thematic Fit F (13 November 2026).

Inference. The direction of demand has improved, but the level of demand is still poor. Growth in the first half of 2027 will look strong against very easy comparisons, so it will prove little. The second half of 2027 is the first honest test of end demand, and visibility beyond it is under two years. GN is not a demand-driven case.

So what. External forces will not produce the upgrades; they set the width of the range of outcomes. One feature helps the holder: the sector currently explains only 8% of GN's daily share-price movement, because corporate events dominate. In the tariff shock of mid-2025 the sector explained about half of GN's movement, and GN moved 1.7 times as far as the sector. GN's insulation from its sector lasts only as long as the cash does.

Strongest counter-case. The headsets bought in 2020-21 are reaching the end of their lives, sales of premium Evolve3 headsets out of the channel are growing at double-digit rates, and Europe may simply lag North America by two or three quarters. If so, revenue growth in 2027 is 5-6%, and each point of growth above consensus adds about 4% to EBITA.

What would change my view. Three signals: positive European Enterprise growth in Q4 2026 before the FalCom deferral; distributors' inventory days falling; and Logitech's late-January results showing European sales out of the channel recovering.

Against the market. Consensus has revenue growing about 5% in 2027; Bernstein has about 2.3% a year for 2027-29. The model, at +2.5% for 2027, sits near the cautious end. I agree with the market that the trough has passed in North America. I disagree that Europe's recovery can yet be put in a base case.

Score: 40, set by the Rater. The external balance is slightly negative for RemainCo: North America and Asia-Pacific have turned and destocking is ending, but Europe (about half of revenue) is still falling, the headset replacement cycle has stretched to four to five years, chief information officers' peripheral budgets grow about 2%, PC shipments are forecast down 8-11% in 2027 and the consumer backdrop for Gaming is weak; consensus sales growth sits at only the 45th percentile and 2026-27 growth flatters on easy comparisons, so I agree with the group score of 38, lifted a touch for the neutralised tariffs and the North American turn, below Carlsberg and above Entra.

#2 Internally-driven corporate change forces, and the absence of problems

Conclusion: The corporate change is large, contracted and dated, and it transforms the per-share figures without yet improving the business underneath them.

≥ DKK 4bn
returned to shareholders by end-2027
DKK 5.5-6.5bn
further returns implied for 2028-2030 by the gearing target
DKK 200m
cost programme, executed in Q2 2026, offsetting stranded cost

Evidence.

  • The sale. Hearing goes to Amplifon for DKK 17.0bn: DKK 12.6bn in cash plus the Amplifon shares. All approvals were met on 6 November 2026, Amplifon completed its financing on 25 November, and closing is expected by end-2026.
  • The return. GN will return at least DKK 4bn by end-2027: up to DKK 1bn by 9 March 2027, then DKK 3bn after the annual general meeting on 10 March. GN is reinstating a dividend of 20-40% of profit. The upfront tax on the sale fell from DKK 1.5-2.0bn to DKK 0.3-0.5bn.
  • The second wave. GN's gearing target of 1.0-1.5 times net debt to EBITDA, on a balance sheet that starts with net cash, implies a further DKK 5.5-6.5bn of returns over 2028-2030. Management has said it will distribute the Amplifon proceeds.
  • The cost programme. The programme saves DKK 200m a year from about 300 roles and was executed in Q2 2026. It offsets the DKK 200m of cost stranded by the sale, so it does not improve the business against its old structure.
  • Discipline. Management rules out large acquisitions in plain words.
  • The problems. GN sold its best and most defensive business and kept the cyclical ones. DNB Carnegie ranks the departure of key employees as the highest risk. The transitional service agreements with Amplifon run for up to 24 months at undisclosed fees, and DNB Carnegie notes a DKK 416m gap between GN's and Amplifon's statements of Hearing's profit, which it attributes to unallocated overhead. The same management team that reversed its "One GN" strategy within two years is still in place, and insiders own less than 0.15% of the shares.

Inference. The corporate change is the strongest part of the case, and its strength is financial. One detail lifts GN above most carve-outs: the cost actions were completed before closing, so the saving and the smaller perimeter arrive together in Q1 2027. In the precedents stranded cost usually lingers: Unilever took three years to remove its stranded cost, and Siemens Healthineers expects its separation costs to arrive years before its savings.

So what. Give high confidence to the lower interest bill, the lower share count and the DKK 200m saving. Give no confidence to the idea that the corporate change makes the franchise stronger. Judge the buyback by the price GN pays for its shares, because the buyback's value to a continuing holder depends on that price.

Strongest counter-case. A second leg of self-help exists that nobody has announced. Administration costs 9% of sales at GN against 3.5% at Logitech, and half-closing that gap is worth DKK 150-250m. Cutting working capital to 25% of revenue would release DKK 0.6-0.7bn. A focused company with net cash can do both. The bear's version is as sharp: management is selling its crown jewel to buy back a cyclical business at 11 times EBITA.

What would change my view. For the better: a quantified second overhead programme or a working-capital target at the Capital Markets Day on 24 February 2027. For the worse: closing slipping into 2027, or the DKK 3bn buyback authorisation delayed or scaled back.

Against the market. The market knows the first DKK 4bn in full. It under-models the second wave: only DNB Carnegie carries a 2028 programme, and no broker sizes 2028-2030. I differ most on the "safety net". Brokers treat GN's cash as a permanent floor under the share price, but the same cash funds the buyback, so it cannot be both.

Score: 77, set by the Rater. A large, funded, mostly contracted reset: Hearing sold for DKK 17bn, more than the whole group was worth, approvals met and closing due by end-2026, at least DKK 4bn returned in 2027 with a further DKK 5.5-6.5bn implied for 2028-30, the interest bill removed and the DKK 200m cost programme already executed, which together take EPS from about 2 to about 8; net of selling the best business, a management team that reversed its strategy, transitional-service and key-staff risks and no improvement to the franchise, it fits the 75 level (separation at a good price, one transaction to close, repair not growth), and I sit above the group's 70 because the per-share effect is among the largest in Europe relative to market value and the closing is all but certain.

#3 Value chain, competitive advantage, financial profile and management

Conclusion: The foundations are one genuine franchise inside a subscale, low-return cost structure, run by a management team that is good at structure and unreliable on demand.

Evidence.

  • One real franchise. Jabra holds about 46% of enterprise headset revenue, against HP Poly's 29% and Logitech's 10%. Certification with Microsoft Teams, Zoom and Google, fleet-management software and 20,000 resellers protect Jabra's position. The Jabra enterprise core is 60-65% of RemainCo.
  • Rational pricing. Through 14 quarters of falling volume the Enterprise gross margin stayed at 55-57%.
  • The diagnostic that matters: overhead, not price. RemainCo's gross margin of about 52% is at or above Logitech's 45-50%, but its EBITA margin is about half Logitech's 14-18%. The gap sits in overhead and in development spending, which runs at about 11% of revenue against Logitech's 6.5%.
  • Weak returns and heavy capital. Return on invested capital was 5.6% in 2025, against about 25% at Logitech. Working capital runs at about 110 days of sales, against 45 at Logitech.
  • Weak flanks. GN's video business has a 3-4% market share. SteelSeries is first in gaming headsets and third in mice and keyboards. One distributor buys about 21% of GN's revenue.
  • Pressure at the edges. Dell launched five certified business headsets in November 2026 at USD 60-140, managed from the same console as its PCs; Jabra's new mid-tier lists at USD 199-389. Yealink earns a 65% gross margin and can fund any price it chooses. Software noise suppression threatens the premium end of the market within 24-36 months.
  • Management. Management is decisive and mostly right on structure: the consumer exit, 31 production lines moved out of China in a year, and the Hearing sale. Management is poor on operating plans: initial growth guidance has been missed every year since 2022. Capital allocation before 2026 was poor: GN bought SteelSeries for DKK 8bn at the peak, then had to raise equity.

Inference. GN's competitive advantage shows in market share and not in returns. A franchise held back by its cost base is more fixable than a weak franchise. But Logitech has three times GN's revenue, so GN's smaller scale caps how far the cost fix can go. A realistic ceiling for GN's EBITA margin is 11-13%.

So what. Value at GN comes from cash yield and cyclical recovery, not from reinvestment at high returns. That source of value caps GN's fair multiple at a cyclical-hardware level (#11).

Strongest counter-case. Jabra, the specialist, has beaten the bundlers for a decade, and took share when HP mishandled its Poly acquisition. The opposite case is a pattern in our Wisdom Library: where a few large players compete, the player that can bundle wins one to two points of share a year, whatever the quality of the single product.

What would change my view. For the worse: the Enterprise underlying gross margin, flat at 55.8% in Q3 2026, starting to fall, which would show GN giving back price. For the better: overhead falling as a share of sales by more than the DKK 200m saving explains.

Against the market. I agree with the market on quality: brokers apply discounts of 22-50% to Logitech's multiple and call RemainCo subscale. I differ in emphasis. The bear narrative is about price and competition. The numbers say GN's problem is overhead, which is the lever management controls.

Score: 39, set by the Rater. One genuine franchise (Jabra about 46% of enterprise headsets, certification barriers, gross margin held at 55-57% through 14 quarters of decline) inside a subscale, cyclical whole: video and Gaming flanks are weak, one distributor buys 21%, Dell bundling and software noise suppression press on the edges, and management is good at structure but has missed operating plans every year; the figures confirm it (return on invested capital 3.3%, 24.7th percentile; net margin 28.9th; capital spending 10.7% of revenue, 81st worst), and new capital is being returned rather than reinvested at high returns, so the groups (60/47/30/40) average about 44 but the low predictability of a cyclical hardware business takes it to just above CVS Group and below IMCD, which has a comparable return but a steadier moat.

#4 Conservatism of guidance, and the record of delivery and upgrades

Conclusion: GN's guidance is conservative on capital return and aggressive on demand, with a record to match, so the path to upgrades runs through the balance sheet and not through operations.

Evidence.

  • The record on demand is poor. Initial organic growth guidance of 2-8% in 2024 produced 1%. In 2025, guidance of 3-7% produced (1)%. In 2026, guidance of 2-8% was cut to 0-6% and then to 0-3%. The only "raise" of 2026, to the margin range, came from tariff refunds; underneath it was a cut of 0.3 points. The share price fell 13% on the day of the February 2026 guidance.
  • The record on what GN controls is good. The earlier group cost programme delivered DKK 600m on schedule. Free cash flow in 2025 was DKK 1.1bn against DKK 0.8bn guided. GN has raised its capital-return ambition twice this year.
  • FY2026 guidance is not yet secure. After (2)% organic growth over nine months, the 0% floor of the range needs about +5% in Q4. I put the chance of landing below the growth range at about 45%, and the chance of landing inside the 9-10% margin range at about 70%, near its bottom.
  • The first FY2027 guidance arrives on 11 February 2027. I expect a growth range about four points wide with a midpoint of 4% or more (about 55% likely), and a margin centred on the finance director's informal 10-11% EBITA. That guidance would put the model's growth in the lower half of the range and its margin at or just under the floor.
  • The Capital Markets Day targets carry a trap of definition. Brokers expect 3-6% growth and a margin of "about 12%", but the measure is unsettled. Guidance is expected to move to EBITDA under the new accounting standard, and GN's EBITDA is only about two points above its EBITA, because amortisation of development cost stays inside EBITDA. A 12% EBITDA target is therefore a 10% EBITA target.

Inference. GN guides ambitiously on what it cannot control, demand, and cautiously on what it can control, cost and capital. That pattern is the opposite of a company that keeps the bar low and beats it. The capital-return wording, "at least", is the one conservative line in GN's guidance.

So what. On Richard's test (conservative guidance, expectations kept low, a record of raising), GN fails on operations and passes on capital. Management could still make the operating bar beatable in one stroke, with a 2027 growth range centred near 3% and a mid-term target defined as a 12% EBITDA margin. The model passes a 10% EBITA margin in 2028, so it would beat a 12% EBITDA target.

Strongest counter-case. A newly standalone company has every reason to start with a bar it can clear, and the chief executive's tone at Q3 2026 was "more tactical". Sonova reset its targets in March 2026 and was beating and raising by November. Logitech set its first-year guidance 1-4% below consensus at its 2025 analyst day.

What would change my view. A 2027 growth midpoint at or below 3%, with a margin floor at or below 9.5% EBITA, would move guidance from a weakness to a strength.

Against the market. The common reading, repeated by Bernstein, is that estimates carry a "credibility discount" to management's targets. They do not. Consensus EBITDA less consensus depreciation gives an EBITA margin of about 10.0%, the bottom of the finance director's range. The gap that investors see is a difference of definition between EBITDA and EBITA.

Score: 28, set by the Rater. Initial organic growth guidance has been missed every year since 2022 (2-8% gave 1% in 2024, 3-7% gave (1)% in 2025, 2026 cut twice to 0-3% with about a 45% chance of a miss) and the only 2026 margin raise came from a tariff refund, while delivery on what GN controls is good (DKK 600m cost programme on time, free cash flow DKK 1.1bn against 0.8bn guided, capital return raised twice); that fits the 25 level of expectations cut in consecutive years, held a little above it by the capital-side record, coherent with the group score of 28 and below Indutrade, whose slippage is shorter.

#5 Pricing power, operating leverage, financial leverage, cost-out and feedback loops

Conclusion: Leverage of every kind is high at GN, but operating leverage is larger on the way down than on the way up, and financial leverage does most of the work.

Evidence and inference, lever by lever.

  • Operating leverage is high and lopsided. About DKK 1.9bn of shared cost, a fifth of revenue, sits below the divisions. Each point of revenue, about DKK 95m, is worth DKK 30-40m of EBITA on the way up, after reinvestment and wage inflation, and DKK 50-60m on the way down, because costs are cut with a lag. GN has not yet shown that leverage on the way up: the Q3 2026 margin, stripped of the tariff refund and an administrative-cost correction, was 8.8%, the same as a year earlier on higher revenue.
  • Pricing power is proven, and used up. GN raised US prices about 10% in 2025 with little loss of volume. That price rise paid for tariffs and is already in the 2026 gross margin. From here price and mix add about 1.2% a year, which roughly covers wages and memory costs. GN prices its new Evolve3 models level with the old ones.
  • Cost-out is in hand, and partly absorbed. About DKK 125m of the DKK 200m saving reaches 2027 EBITA after reinvestment in launches. More saving is possible (#2), but none is promised.
  • Financial leverage is reversed, then rebuilt on purpose. Net financial items swing from about (DKK 540m) in 2026 to about +DKK 50m in 2027. GN then borrows again towards its gearing target, which adds both to EPS and to risk.
  • The dominant feedback loop is financial. The sale proceeds buy shares, and fewer shares raise EPS. The loop has two brakes: the buyback retires fewer shares as GN's share price rises, and the size of the 2028 wave depends on Amplifon's share price.

So what. Revenue growth does lead to outsized profit growth: one point of revenue moves EBITA about 4% up or 6% down. Two less obvious consequences matter more.

  • EPS grows strongly even without revenue growth. With no organic growth at all in 2027, EBITA is about DKK 820-840m and EPS is only about 8% below the base case.
  • The buyback raises each share's exposure to the cycle. By 2028 the same swing in profit is spread over about 30% fewer shares, so the sensitivity of EPS to revenue rises by about 40%. Steady buyback-driven growth will make GN's EPS look smoother than the business underneath it is.
Strongest counter-case. Drop-through on the way up could beat 30-40% if management banks the DKK 200m saving and does not reinvest it. That is the route by which a modest revenue beat becomes a large profit beat.

What would change my view. Two consecutive quarters of growth with underlying drop-through above 40%.

Against the market. Brokers describe GN's leverage in general terms. I find no broker that states the asymmetry, or that notes that the buyback increases cyclicality per share.

Score: 57, set by the Rater. The structure has real but lopsided gearing: about DKK 1.9bn of shared fixed cost means one point of revenue moves EBITA about 4% up (30-40% drop-through, not yet shown in Q3) and about 6% down, pricing power was proven once with the 2025 US price rise but is now used up (price and mix about 1.2% a year), cost-out is partly absorbed (DKK 125m of 200m reaching EBITA) and the dominant loop is financial, with interest removal and buybacks amplifying EPS and re-gearing towards 1.0-1.5x adding to it; the huge forecast EPS-to-revenue ratio is mostly that financial engineering, so this is the 50 level of asymmetric leverage without fresh pricing power, lifted into the high 50s for the size of the fixed block and the deliberate financial leverage (coherent with Financial forecasts 70 and Economic strength 30).

#6 Forecast financials

Conclusion: The forecasts show ordinary revenue growth, a real but bounded margin recovery and extraordinary per-share growth. The per-share growth is the most dependable line because it is contracted; the revenue line is the least dependable because it rests on European demand.

How to read the forecasts.

  • Double-digit growth: yes per share, just about in operating profit, no in revenue. EBITA grows about 10% a year from 2027 to 2030. Revenue grows at the market's rate, with GN's market share flat.
  • The margin improves on the past, within limits. The EBITA margin rises 3.7 points from the underlying 2026 level: about 1.3 points from the cost saving, about 2.5 points from volume spread over fixed cost, and nothing from price. That improvement beats RemainCo's recent record and stays well short of the 15-17% the old Audio business earned.
  • The EPS bridge from 2026 to 2028 is mostly financial. Of the rise in like-for-like EPS, about half comes from the interest bill disappearing, about a third from the lower share count and about a fifth from operations.
  • Three cautions on the model's figures.
    • Model EPS divides net income by fewer shares than a time-weighted average gives: about 122 million against 129 million in 2027, and 63 million against 73 million in 2030. On time-weighted shares, model EPS for 2027-2030 is 5.73, 7.67, 9.59 and 11.49. The earlier Analyst's note asking for the model to be corrected is still open.
    • FY2026 free cash flow of DKK 2,137m is not cash generated by the business. It is Hearing's working capital leaving with the business. The underlying figure is about (DKK 315m).
    • The model holds capital spending at DKK 720-750m a year. Consensus has it falling to about DKK 500m by 2029, which would need either cuts to development or a change of accounting.
  • My one change to the model's inputs. The existing inputs borrow enough for buybacks to take net debt to about 1.6-1.7 times EBITDA on the company's own definition by end-2030, above GN's 1.0-1.5 times target. A base case should sit inside the company's stated policy. I have therefore trimmed the 2029 and 2030 buybacks by DKK 250m each, with the interest cost that goes with them, so that 2028-2030 returns total DKK 6.0bn, the middle of the range the target implies, and gearing ends 2030 at about 1.35 times. The change lowers model EPS by about 1% in FY2029 and 3% in FY2030, and changes nothing before 2029.
Strongest counter-case. The forecasts may be too cautious on the top line: consensus revenue is 3-4% higher in 2027-2029. Or they may be too generous on margin: the clean Q3 2026 margin showed no progress, and a second layer of standalone cost may appear when the transitional service agreements end in late 2028.

What would change my view. FY2027 guidance and Q1 2027 results together will show whether the model's +2.5% growth and 9.4% margin are low or high. The annual report on 11 February 2027 settles leases, debt terms and the accounting for the Amplifon stake.

Against the market. For 2027 the model is below consensus by about 3% on revenue and by about 5-9% on EBITA. For 2028 it is about 8% above consensus on like-for-like EPS, and its dividends are more than double consensus. The 2027 EPS consensus is not a usable yardstick: broker EPS figures run from about 1 to nearly 5 on EBITA forecasts within 7% of each other, and my sources even disagree on the share counts brokers assume. For the same reason, the model summary's own comparison (EPS 55% and EBITDA 22% above consensus in 2027) mixes bases and is not a statement of view.

Score: 62, set by the Rater. The four-year rate is far above 35%, so C, though it rests on a FY2026 base depressed by the interest bill on debt that leaves with Hearing; even from FY2027 model EPS grows about 30% a year (26% on time-weighted shares) while net income grows only about 4% and EBITA about 10%, so almost all of it is bought with the balance sheet. I place it in the upper half of the band because the mechanical part is contracted and dated and the EBITA margin rises 3.7 points to 11.3%, above RemainCo's recent record, but not higher because the organic part is ordinary (revenue +2.5-3.5%).

#7 Scope for upgrades to guidance, estimates and narrative over 6-12 months

Conclusion: Upgrades are likely where they are mechanical or about capital, and unlikely where they would matter most, in revenue and operating profit.

Evidence: the likely direction of each line.

Inference. EPS estimates and operating estimates are set to move in opposite directions, and the order of events matters.

  • Until February 2027: the sale closes, the first buyback data arrive and EPS estimates rise mechanically, which will look like momentum.
  • In February 2027: two operating tests arrive two weeks apart, the results with the first FY2027 guidance and the Capital Markets Day targets.
  • Through 2027: capital news is good, and operating revisions lean down.
  • From late 2027: the Amplifon share sale and the second return programme arrive, the largest positive not yet in estimates, just as the cash floor is used up.

So what. The scope for upgrades is real, but most of it is not the kind that earns a re-rating. In the sector's precedents a higher multiple follows volume growth, and EPS growth driven by a falling share count is not volume growth. The single most valuable surprise would be a low bar set in February 2027 (#4), because a low bar would turn likely operating downgrades into possible upgrades.

How the narrative can improve. Today's story is "the buyback is coming". Once the buyback starts, the question becomes "what is RemainCo worth?". The story can improve through a second return programme, through the buyback absorbing William Demant Invest's 12-14% holding instead of leaving it to hang over the shares, or through break-up options.
How the narrative can sour. The story can sour through "sell the news", through a mid-term margin target read as low ambition against the old 16-17% margin, or through the theme "software kills the headset".
Strongest counter-case. If Q4 2026 shows Enterprise growing despite the FalCom deferral, Gaming has a strong holiday season and guidance is set with room to beat, then operating leverage works in favour of the estimates.

What would change my view. Consensus sales estimates for 2027, unchanged for three months, starting to rise.

Against the market. The dashboard's sell-side momentum rating may improve on EPS and target-price revisions alone. I would not read that improvement as a fundamental signal. The evidence on what investors, as distinct from brokers, are saying is thin, but what there is suggests investors focus entirely on the buyback.

Score: 48, set by the Rater. Guidance, which counts most, pulls both ways: the 'at least' DKK 4bn capital return is about 65% likely to be raised, but the first FY2027 growth guidance is likely set near consensus and is 50% likely to be cut during 2027, as it was in each recent year; 2027 EPS consensus should rise mechanically in the next three months as brokers remove the old interest bill and 2028 EPS should rise when the next buyback is described (the model is 13% and 8% above consensus), but 2027 revenue and EBITA consensus is 55-60% likely to fall, and the narrative risks 'sell the news', so this is upgrades on one part and downgrades on another, slightly above the group's 40 for the size of the mechanical EPS gap against about 3-5% revenue growth, just below Kerry.

So what. The momentum has one solid prop through 2027: GN itself will buy about 20% of daily trading volume. The buyback supports the share price, but it does not make the fundamentals catch up.

Strongest counter-case. Momentum can feed itself. Closing, weekly buyback reports and rising EPS estimates could lift the dashboard's D rating for sell-side momentum and draw in buyers who follow revisions.

What would change my view. Sales revisions turning positive and the share of buy ratings recovering, together.

Against the market. I have no difference of fact with the market, only a difference of reading. The market sees rising EPS estimates; I see unchanged sales estimates.

Score: 63, set by the Rater. One measure positive and one negative gives C; the negative sell-side score is partly an artefact of Hearing leaving the numbers (three-month FY2027 EPS +12%, EBITDA +5%, target prices +8%), the price is 16% above a young 200-day average and capital guidance was raised twice, but sales estimates are flat, the share of buy ratings fell 12 points in a month and peers are soft, so the parts do not strongly contradict the measures and I place it in the upper half of the band, beside Storskogen.

#9 Riskiness and simplicity of the forecasts

Conclusion: The case is simple in shape, complicated in its accounts, well protected until early 2028 and progressively riskier after it, and one judgement, the multiple, outweighs all the others.

The architecture of the case is simple; the accounts are not. The case is a firm financial layer on a soft operating layer. The accounts, by contrast, are complicated. Three definitions of EBITDA are in use. The company defines no adjusted EPS. Guidance changes its measure in the same quarter as the perimeter changes. The accounting treatment of the Amplifon stake is undecided, and it can move reported profit by about DKK 470m for each 10% move in Amplifon's share price. The first clean year-on-year comparison arrives in 2028.

The five judgements, with the arithmetic.

1. Europe delivers enough volume for revenue to grow 2.5% in 2027. Plausible error: 3 points.

  • 3 points of 2026 revenue of DKK 9,443m is DKK 283m.
  • On a shortfall, 55% drops through: EBITA falls by DKK 156m, from 911 to 755, a margin of 8.0%.
  • No interest bill remains to absorb any of the shortfall. Net income falls by 156 × 77% = DKK 120m, from 740 to 620.
  • Over the model's 122 million shares, DKK 120m is DKK 0.98 a share: model EPS falls from 6.06 to 5.08, or 16%. Like-for-like EPS falls from 4.42 to 3.49, or 21%, because the acquisition amortisation is a fixed deduction.
  • The lower base carries forward: 2028 model EPS falls by 120 × 1.035 ÷ 95 million shares = 1.30, to 6.92.
  • On the upside, 35% drops through: EBITA rises DKK 99m to 1,010 (a 10.1% margin, where consensus sits), net income rises DKK 76m, and model EPS rises 0.62 to 6.68, or 10%.

2. The margin holds: the gross margin stays near 52% and DKK 125m of the saving reaches profit. Plausible error: 1 point of margin.

  • 1 point of 2027 revenue is DKK 97m of EBITA (EBITA of 814 or 1,008).
  • Net income moves by 97 × 77% = DKK 75m.
  • Model EPS moves by 0.61, or 10%; like-for-like EPS moves by 0.58, or 13%.
  • GN loses a point if European entry and mid-tier prices give back 2-3% (about DKK 50m) and launch, channel or transitional costs run DKK 45m over plan. GN gains a point if the saving arrives in full (+DKK 75m) and memory costs ease.

3. GN buys back its shares near today's price. The model's share count fits a constant price of about DKK 120 (the earlier Analyst's inference; the model does not state it). Plausible error: DKK 140 in 2027 and DKK 160 in 2028 if the shares re-rate, or DKK 100 if they sag.

  • At DKK 120, the DKK 3,850m and DKK 3,000m spent in 2027 and 2028 retire 32.1m + 25.0m = 57.1m shares.
  • At DKK 140 and 160 the same sums retire 27.5m + 18.8m = 46.3m shares, which is 10.8m fewer.
  • 2029 model EPS becomes 806 ÷ (76.7m + 10.8m) = 9.21, against 10.51: 12% lower.
  • At DKK 100 the same sums retire 68.5m shares, which is 11.4m more: 806 ÷ 65.3m = 12.35, 17% higher.
  • The buyback price therefore stabilises value per share. It is also why the forecast EPS and a large re-rating cannot both happen.

4. The Amplifon shares realise DKK 4.0bn (about DKK 4.7bn at the early-November price). Plausible error: 20%.

  • 20% of DKK 4.0bn is DKK 0.8bn, or DKK 5.5 a GN share today, 4.6% of the price.
  • If GN cuts buybacks to match, 0.8bn ÷ DKK 120 = 6.7m fewer shares are retired: 2029 model EPS is 806 ÷ 83.4m = 9.66, 8% lower.
  • If GN borrows instead, net debt is DKK 0.8bn higher, about 0.6 times EBITDA on the company's definition, and interest of about DKK 36m takes 3.5% off net income.

5. The multiple the market pays once the cash has become fewer shares.

  • At March 2028, two-year-forward EPS is 11.08 on the model's basis and about 8.4 like for like.
  • Each turn of multiple is worth DKK 11 a share on the model's basis and DKK 8.4 like for like: 9% and 7% of today's price.
  • The guideline gives 24.79 × 11.08 = DKK 275. My central view gives 15 × 8.4 = DKK 126. The difference, DKK 149, is more than today's whole share price, and more than the other four judgements together.

Fragilities: the volume judgement rests on narrow foundations. Enterprise in Europe alone is 36% of group revenue. One product family, Evolve3, covers half of Enterprise. One distributor buys a fifth of sales. The fourth quarter brings about 31% of revenue and 35% of EBITA. GN also built DKK 205m of inventory for a fourth quarter that must grow 5%; if distributors take that inventory and then cut stock at their year-end, Q1 2027 sales will pay for it.

Suddenness and trackability: better than GN's record suggests.

  • Weekly: shares bought and prices paid. Daily: Amplifon's share price.
  • Ahead of GN's own reports: Logitech's results in late January, HP, Dell and PC shipment data.
  • Sudden shocks: a tariff change on Vietnam or Malaysia (one to two points of margin), a purge of stock at the big distributor, or a chip shortage. Logitech's own supply failure was first sized at USD 200m and ended at USD 70-80m; such shocks tend to halve within a quarter.
  • Sentiment shocks: two results events within two weeks in February on a share that has already run; a price-to-earnings multiple at the 99th percentile of its five-year range; and short interest that reached 12% of the free float in 2025.
So what: the risk is dated. A fair trough value today is about DKK 75-90 a share, 25-37% below the model's price: RemainCo at 6-7 times trough EBITA plus the non-operating assets marked down. By early 2028 GN will have spent those assets on shares. From then the floor is whatever a cyclical business with debt is worth, and GN's sensitivity to its sector should return towards the 1.7 times seen in 2025.

What the precedents say.

PrecedentWhat happened
On cyclicalityLogitech's sales fell 17% in a quarter and its gross margin fell to 37.9% in the bust of 2022-23. An 8% organic decline once cut GN's group EBITA by 44% (Morgan Stanley).
On leveragePlantronics, the leveraged, subscale number two, lost share and was sold at a depressed price.
On buybacksBuybacks funded from cash in hand were delivered (Logitech, Demant). Buybacks funded from debt or future cash flow were cut when operations weakened (HP after Poly, Teleperformance). GN's programme is funded from cash in hand in 2027, from an asset at a market price in 2028 and from debt in 2029-2030.
On re-ratingBuybacks funded by a disposal re-rated a share for good where the remaining business was the better one (ABB, Trelleborg). Where organic growth was negative the rallies faded (Teleperformance: +55%, then +22%, then +19%).
Strongest counter-case. Demand, the line on which management's record is unreliable, produces under a fifth of the EPS change, so the forecast is safer than its author's history implies. I accept that argument for the direction of EPS, but not for its level: around its centre, 2027 like-for-like EPS has a range of about (28)% to +18%, as wide as EBITA's, because nothing below operating profit cushions it any more.

What would change my view. Within six months, hard data will show whether the financial layer has been delivered: closing, about 8-9 million shares retired by March 2027, and the DKK 3bn authorisation. Any slip in those three would move the case from average to high risk.

Against the market. The market treats the cash as a permanent floor and the range of EPS outcomes as narrow. I think the floor has an end date and the range of EPS outcomes is wide and skewed down.

Score: 41, set by the Rater. The architecture is simple (a firm financial layer on a soft operating one) and weekly trackable, with net cash and a fair trough of DKK 75-90 protecting the holder until early 2028, but the memo's 2027 like-for-like EPS range is about (28)% to +18%, skewed down, nothing below EBITA cushions an operating miss any more, the accounts are complicated (three EBITDA definitions, undecided Amplifon accounting, no clean comparison until 2028), the drivers are concentrated (European Enterprise 36% of revenue, one distributor 21%, Q4 35% of EBITA) and the multiple alone outweighs every other judgement; between the group scores of 44 and 58, I sit just below Rexel because the range is wider and the cyclicality higher, above D'Ieteren because the balance sheet is about to hold net cash.

#10 Where the stock is in its lifecycle

Conclusion: GN is Turning up in its fundamentals and already Broadening in its share price, which leaves the price ahead of the proof.

Evidence.

  • The dashboard's rule puts GN's starting Phase at Broadening.
  • The multiple's own history explains part of that reading. The two-year-forward price-to-earnings multiple went from 8.9x in July 2026 to 19.5x in August with the share price flat at about DKK 97, because consensus earnings were re-based for the smaller company. The market did not pay more for GN; the earnings in the denominator shrank. The 20% rise in the share price since August is the genuine re-rating.
  • The operating business has had one quarter of growth after 14 quarters of decline.
  • The market's behaviour (#8) is that of a share late in a first re-rating: a rising price, a falling share of buy ratings and flat sales estimates.

Inference. GN runs on two clocks. The capital-return thesis is Broadening: every broker has it, and the price has moved. The operating thesis is only Turning up, and unproven. The share price is one phase ahead of the estimates.

So what. In a share in true Broadening, upgrades spread from a few analysts to many, and from one line to several. At GN upgrades are spreading in EPS only, for reasons unrelated to the business. The operating phase is the one that matters for the multiple, so I read GN as Turning up, with forecasts that are still uncertain.

The paths from here. To genuine Broadening: sales estimates rising, Europe turning and the share of buy ratings recovering. To Stalling: FY2027 guidance set high and cut at Q1 or Q2, as in 2025 and 2026. Collapsing would need a European freeze after the cash has been spent, which makes it a 2028 risk, not a 2027 one.

Strongest counter-case. The market does not distinguish between kinds of EPS growth while the growth is running, so Broadening in the share price could continue through 2027 on buybacks alone.

What would change my view. A second half of 2027 with Enterprise growth of 3% or more against normal comparisons.

Against the market. The dashboard says Broadening by rule. The sell-side's ratings say the first leg of the re-rating is largely done. I side with the sell-side's reading for the operations and with the dashboard's reading for the price.

Score: 54, set by the Rater. I agree with the memo and the computed Turning/Inflecting rather than the dashboard's Broadening: the operating business has one quarter of growth after 14 of decline and sales estimates are flat, while the price has already re-rated 20% and behaves like a late first leg (falling buy share, P/E at a five-year high), so the capital thesis is late Broadening in the price and the operating thesis early and unproven; that is short of the attractive early Turning because the price is ahead of the proof, between Greggs and Solid State.

#11 The fair multiple

Conclusion: The guideline's 24.79x is a hearing-aid multiple; a fair multiple for RemainCo once the cash is spent is 14-16x like-for-like earnings.

The guideline. For a stock in Broadening, Viewforth's guideline sets the fair multiple at the 80th percentile of the stock's own ten-year range of two-year-forward price-to-earnings multiples: 24.79x for GN, against 21.77x now. Topic #12 uses the guideline multiple.

My view: the guideline multiple is too high for the company GN has become, for three reasons.

  1. The history belongs to a different company. Every month in which GN traded above about 23x fell between mid-2018 and mid-2021, when GN was a hearing-aid group enjoying a pandemic audio boom and group margins of 13-17%. From April 2022 to July 2026, as a leveraged, hardware-led group, GN traded between 6.5x and 15.5x.
  2. Today's multiple is a snapshot of a balance sheet in transit. About 45% of the price is cash and securities that do not yet show fully in earnings. As the cash becomes fewer shares, forward EPS rises and the multiple falls with no change in the price. At an unchanged share price the like-for-like multiple drops from about 21x today to about 14x by March 2028. Holding 24.79x at that date is therefore not the 14% re-rating it looks like today. It means paying about three quarters more than an unchanged price implies, for earnings that have already absorbed the cash.
  3. Peers and phase point lower. Logitech, with twice GN's margin, net cash and all development cost expensed, trades at about 17x forward earnings. In its own first year of recovery Logitech reached 22-23x and fell back to 18x within months, when growth expectations moderated while margins were still beating. Brokers value RemainCo at about 10-10.5 times operating profit, and apply discounts of a fifth to a half to Logitech's multiple. The guideline's own logic also gives a lower multiple to a stock that is Turning up (#10).
So what. The multiple is the largest single swing in the return (#9, #12), so the choice of which history to draw the multiple from matters more than any forecast.

My range: 14-16x two-year-forward like-for-like EPS at the 18-month point, with 15x as the centre. That range sits between the 35th percentile (14.0x) and the median (16.8x) of the ten-year range, and equals about 9.5-11 times EBITA for RemainCo. It is above the 11x five-year median because the debt is gone and the company is simpler. On the model's own EPS basis the same value is about 10.5-12x.

The range of outcomes for the multiple. 17-18x, Logitech's level, if 2027 proves volume growth. 11-12x if Europe weakens.

Strongest counter-case. A net-cash company growing EPS at 25-30% a year can hold a growth multiple for as long as the growth runs, and disposal-funded buybacks did re-rate ABB and Trelleborg for good. My answer is that in those cases the remaining business was the better one. At GN the remaining business is the more cyclical one, and the EPS growth is bought with the balance sheet.

What would change my view. Two years of organic growth at 4% or better, with the EBITA margin above 11%, would justify 17-18x.

Against the market. On the multiple I am with the market and against the guideline. Jefferies notes that about 20x 2027 earnings is an 18% premium to Logitech, where GN has usually traded at a discount. Even DNB Carnegie, the most positive broker with detailed forecasts, reaches its DKK 135 target by valuing RemainCo at about 10.5 times its 2027 EBITA.

Score: 32, set by the Rater. Neutral on one measure and dear on the other gives D. The neutral own-range reading flatters, because every month above about 23x belongs to the hearing-aid group of 2018-21 and the business left is the more cyclical one, so it deserves less than its own history (it traded at 6.5-15.5x from 2022 to mid-2026), and the like-for-like multiple of about 21x sits well above the memo's fair 14-16x; I place it in the lower part of the band.

Conclusion: The model's +130% is a statement about the guideline multiple. On a multiple suited to the business the return is about +6% over 18 months and about 10% a year over three years, within a roughly symmetric range of outcomes.

What drives the model's return.

  • Earnings: nearly all of the earnings leg is fewer shares. Two-year-forward model EPS rises from about 7.4 today to about 11.1 at March 2028 and 14.5 at September 2029. Over the first step net income rises only about 5%, while the share count falls about 29%.
  • The multiple rises from 16.1x today, on the model's EPS, to 24.79x.
  • Dividends are small, because management prefers buybacks: DKK 0.85 and then DKK 1.60 a share.

Three cautions when using the model's return.

  1. The two multiples are on different bases. The guideline's 24.79x comes from a history measured on consensus earnings, on which GN stands at 21.77x today: a gap of 14%. The model sets 24.79x against 16.1x on its own, higher, EPS: a gap of 54%. About 40 points of the multiple leg come from that mismatch.
  2. The earnings leg and the multiple leg cannot both be delivered. The share count behind the earnings leg assumes buybacks at about DKK 120. If the shares were worth DKK 275, the DKK 3bn spent in 2028 would retire about 11 million shares, not 25 million. The more the share price re-rates, the less the share count falls (#9, judgement 3).
  3. The guideline multiple itself is too high for RemainCo (#11).

  • The central return is modest although EPS doubles, because half the price earns almost nothing. A holder today owns RemainCo for a little over half the price and low-yielding cash and securities for the rest. RemainCo's profit grows about 10% a year, and RemainCo generates cash. The cash and securities earn almost nothing until GN spends them, and spent at fair value they add no value. The blend is a return of roughly 10% a year, not the 30% a year at which EPS grows.
  • Higher EPS would not make the return much better; three other things would. A lower buyback price, because each krone spent below intrinsic value transfers value to continuing holders; RemainCo's profit growing faster than 10% a year; or proof of volume growth that earns the higher multiple.

Strongest counter-case. The guideline multiple could prove right for a period: if the market capitalises EPS growth without asking where it comes from, a multiple in the low twenties on rising EPS is possible during 2027. I would treat such a multiple as a price ahead of value, not as fair value.

What would change my view. The evidence set out in #11 that would justify 17-18x.

Against the market. The brokers' mean and median target prices are DKK 124 and DKK 130, and my central value of about DKK 127 matches them. The model's DKK 275 is the outlier, and it is an outlier because of the multiple, not because of the forecasts.

Score: 36, set by the Rater. About +4% maps to about 35 and falls in D; I lift it a point because the three-year check is about 10% a year and the dashboard's lower price adds about four points, and hold it there because the lower tail ((25)% to (37)% in a European freeze) is as fat as the upper and the earnings leg is offset by a de-rating to the fair multiple; the model's +130% rests on a guideline multiple the memo rejects.

#13 Summary conclusion

GN has done the hard, valuable thing. It sold a business for more than the whole group was worth, cleared its debt, and committed to hand the proceeds back to shareholders. That part of the case is as dependable as anything in European mid-caps: dated, contracted, trackable every week, and largely independent of a hostile sector. It transforms EPS.

The capital return does not transform the business, and the business is what the earnings will be valued on once the cash has gone. RemainCo has one real franchise, a cost base too heavy for its scale, a demand record that has disappointed every year, and a recovery that is one quarter old in two regions. Consensus estimates leave RemainCo no cushion to beat, and the share price has already paid for the first year of the capital return.

Strongly positive: capital return and per-share mechanics, which the market mostly knows.
Negative: operating expectations, which is where a re-rating would have to come from.

The skew Richard looks for is present, but for now it sits in the wrong place. The case becomes genuinely skewed to the positive if February 2027 delivers a low bar, if Europe turns, or if the share price falls far enough for the buyback to create value rather than merely convert cash into fewer shares. Each of those three triggers is observable, and two of them are dated within three months.

Thesis's Change Forces' Strength: 72, set by the Rater. A very large, funded and dated internal change (topic 2 at 77) reaches profits with near certainty, net income nearly tripling in 2027 as the interest bill goes and EPS compounding about 30% a year from 2027 (topic 6), but the external forces are slightly negative (topic 1 at 40) and the change does not improve the franchise, so operating profit grows only about 10% a year; that is a clear positive with one weak part, at the lower end of the 75 level and below Munters' broader organic change.

Foundations' Robustness: 37, set by the Rater. One genuine certification-protected franchise and a balance sheet about to hold net cash sit inside a subscale, cyclical, low-return business (topic 3 at 39), and the delivery record on demand guidance is poor (topic 4 at 28), so it sits between the 25 level of a narrow moat with returns below the cost of capital and missed targets and the 50 level of good unit moats with a strong balance sheet, above Maersk and Alfen because the Jabra moat holds price.

Setups' Fit/Crispness: 66, set by the Rater. The case fits 'Big Corporate Change-driven EPSU' in substance: the corporate change is large, contracted and dated and it drives a step-up in EPS from about 2 to about 8 with net income rising, not falling; the fit is blurred by today's operating problems (demand guidance missed every year, Europe still falling, operating estimates leaning down) and by the change leaving the business itself unimproved, so it is a clear fit with one current problem, below 75. I set aside the memo's point that the step-up is widely known and priced, which belongs to topics 7 and 12.

Case Riskiness: 42, set by the Rater. Following topic 9 at 41, the cash and securities (about 45% of the price), contracted events and weekly trackability constrain the risk until early 2028, but the wide, downward-skewed operating cone, complicated accounts, a cyclical business with concentrated drivers, a multiple at a five-year high and the return to a geared claim after 2028 put it below the 50 level, beside Helios Towers.

End notes

Definitions. Money is in DKK. "RemainCo" is the company after the Hearing sale: Enterprise (Jabra office headsets, video, FalCom tactical headsets) and Gaming (SteelSeries). "EBITA" is the company's adjusted EBITA: before amortisation of the intangibles bought with SteelSeries and before special items. Two bases of earnings per share (EPS) appear, and each is always labelled. Model EPS is the Financial Analyst's model, before that amortisation and before special items. Like-for-like EPS is after that amortisation, on time-weighted shares, the basis closest to broker consensus.

Prices and sources. The model's share price is DKK 119.60 (19 November 2026); the dashboard's is DKK 114.9 (20 November 2026). The latest Earnings Review covers Q3 2026, reported on 5 November 2026; I checked that date against the review itself.

Visuals. Charts drawn for this page (visuals/drawn and visuals/drawn-copy-editor) take their figures from the memo; where the memo gives a range, the chart shows its midpoint and says so. Default visuals not used: the ten-year financials table (its figures are in the annual history and consensus tables and the financial trajectory chart), Viewforth against consensus line by line (it mixes bases, as #6 explains) and consensus revisions by period (its figures are in the sell-side chart in #8).

Appendix: a comment from the Financial Analyst on reporting basis

Our model keeps one reporting basis for history and forecasts. The checks below suggest that consensus may use a different basis for some lines, so part of the gap between our forecasts and consensus on those lines may not be a difference of view. Nothing has been adjusted in the model.

What the checks found:

  • Consensus net income for FY2026 is (371.50), (152.3)% against 711.00 in FY2025 on our model's basis; consensus revenue moves (43.7)%.

Facts in the data file that commonly explain such a gap:

  • Hybrid bond coupons and capitalised leases are not in the data file; check the company's reporting where relevant.
